# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Trip::calculateMonthlyPoints
Summary: Computes the total reward points earned by a given customer across bookings of this trip within the requested month. Each booked seat contributes 5 points and only customers whose membership package contains the POINTS award are eligible.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null OR currentMonth is null/empty, return 0.
  2. If customer.membershipPackage is null OR not customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS), return 0.
  3. Initialize total = 0.
  4. For each booking b in this.bookings:
       a. If b is null, skip.
       b. If b.customer == customer AND b.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true, total += b.numberOfSeats * 5.
  5. Return total.
Related Features: bookings
Related Classes: Customer, Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
Input:
  - customer : Customer - the customer whose points are being calculated; must be non-null.
  - currentMonth : String - a textual month identifier, e.g., "yyyy-MM"; must be non-null and non-empty.
Output: int - the total points earned for the given month by the given customer; 0 if the customer is not eligible or no bookings qualify.
Pre-condition: Bookings on this trip, if any, are valid Booking instances referencing the same customer instance and have parseable bookingDate values.
Post-condition: No state change occurs.

Trip::bookSeats
Summary: Attempts to commit a seat reservation on this trip by reducing the available seat count. It returns true if the seats were successfully reserved, and false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If num <= 0, return false.
  2. Compute booked = this.getBookedSeats().
  3. If booked + num > this.numberOfSeats, return false.
  4. Decrement this.numberOfSeats by num.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats
Related Classes: None
Input:
  - num : int - the number of seats to reserve; must be a positive integer.
Output: boolean - true if seats were reserved; false if num is non-positive or there are not enough seats.
Pre-condition: The trip has a valid positive numberOfSeats and the bookings list is consistent with the current seat inventory.
Post-condition: On success, this.numberOfSeats is reduced by num; on failure, no state change occurs.

Trip::getStopStations
Summary: Returns a list containing the names of all stop stations declared for this indirect trip. For direct trips (with no stops), the returned list is empty.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty list result.
  2. If stops is null or empty, return result (empty list).
  3. For each Stop s in stops, if s is not null and s.stopStation is not null, add s.stopStation to result.
  4. Return result.
Related Features: stops
Related Classes: Stop
Input: None
Output: List<String> - a list of stop station names in the order they appear in the stops collection; empty if the trip has no stops.
Pre-condition: The stops list, if present, contains valid Stop instances with non-null stopStation strings.
Post-condition: No state change occurs; the returned list may be a new list and is safe for the caller to iterate.

Trip::calculateDiscountedPrice
Summary: Computes the final price for a booking made by a given customer at a given booking time. A 20 percent discount is applied only if the customer's membership package contains the DISCOUNTS award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before the trip's departure time (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary). The result is rounded to one decimal place.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null OR bookingTime is null OR this.departureTime is null, return this.price.
  2. If customer.membershipPackage is null OR not customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS), return this.price.
  3. Parse bookingTime and this.departureTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"; if parsing fails, return this.price.
  4. Compute the duration in minutes between bookingTime and departureTime.
  5. If duration < 24 * 60 (i.e., less than 24 hours before departure), return this.price.
  6. Compute discounted = this.price * 0.8.
  7. Round discounted to one decimal place (e.g., using Math.round(discounted * 10) / 10.0).
  8. Return discounted.
Related Features: price, departureTime
Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
Input:
  - customer : Customer - the booking customer; must be non-null to receive a discount.
  - bookingTime : String - the booking datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format; must be non-null and parseable.
Output: double - the final price after potential discount, rounded to one decimal place; if no discount applies, the original price is returned.
Pre-condition: The trip's price and departureTime are set; the customer's membership package, if present, contains valid Award values.
Post-condition: No state change occurs; the computation is read-only.

Trip::isTimeConflicting
Summary: Determines whether a candidate time window overlaps with this trip's scheduled time window. Overlap is defined as the intervals sharing any positive duration; identical intervals are considered conflicting, but an exact boundary touch (e.g., one trip ends exactly when the other starts) is allowed.
Algorithm:
  1. Try to parse this.departureTime, this.arrivalTime, newDepartureTime, and newArrivalTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"; if any parsing fails, return false.
  2. If this.departureTime >= this.arrivalTime OR newDepartureTime >= newArrivalTime, return false.
  3. Return (this.departureTime < newArrivalTime) AND (newDepartureTime < this.arrivalTime).
Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
Related Classes: None
Input:
  - newDepartureTime : String - the proposed departure time in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format.
  - newArrivalTime : String - the proposed arrival time in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format; must be strictly later than newDepartureTime.
Output: boolean - true if the candidate interval overlaps this trip's interval (strict intersection); false otherwise.
Pre-condition: This trip's departureTime and arrivalTime are valid datetime strings; the proposed times are also valid datetime strings.
Post-condition: No state change occurs; the method is read-only.

Trip::getBookedSeats
Summary: Aggregates the total number of seats already reserved across all bookings associated with this trip.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize total = 0.
  2. If bookings is null or empty, return 0.
  3. For each booking b in bookings, if b is not null, total += b.numberOfSeats.
  4. Return total.
Related Features: bookings
Related Classes: Booking
Input: None
Output: int - the sum of numberOfSeats across all bookings on this trip; 0 if no bookings exist.
Pre-condition: The bookings list, if present, contains valid Booking instances whose numberOfSeats is a non-negative integer.
Post-condition: No state change occurs; the method is read-only.

   * Summary: Computes the final price for a booking made by a given customer at a given booking time. A 20 percent discount is applied only if the customer's membership package contains the DISCOUNTS award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before the trip's departure time (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary). The result is rounded to one decimal place.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null OR bookingTime is null OR this.departureTime is null, return this.price.
   *   2. If customer.membershipPackage is null OR not customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS), return this.price.
   *   3. Parse bookingTime and this.departureTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"; if parsing fails, return this.price.
   *   4. Compute the duration in minutes between bookingTime and departureTime.
   *   5. If duration < 24 * 60 (i.e., less than 24 hours before departure), return this.price.
   *   6. Compute discounted = this.price * 0.8.
   *   7. Round discounted to one decimal place (e.g., using Math.round(discounted * 10) / 10.0).
   *   8. Return discounted.
   * Related Features: price, departureTime
   * Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input:
   *   - customer : Customer - the booking customer; must be non-null to receive a discount.
   *   - bookingTime : String - the booking datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format; must be non-null and parseable.
   * Output: double - the final price after potential discount, rounded to one decimal place; if no discount applies, the original price is returned.
   * Pre-condition: The trip's price and departureTime are set; the customer's membership package, if present, contains valid Award values.
   * Post-condition: No state change occurs; the computation is read-only.

   * @generated NOT
   */
  public double calculateDiscountedPrice(final Customer customer, final String bookingTime)
  {
    if (customer == null || bookingTime == null || getDepartureTime() == null)
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS))
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
    SimpleDateFormat format = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    try
    {
      Date bookingDate = format.parse(bookingTime);
      Date departureDate = format.parse(getDepartureTime());
      long durationMinutes = (departureDate.getTime() - bookingDate.getTime()) / (60 * 1000);
      if (durationMinutes < 24 * 60)
      {
        return getPrice();
      }
      double discounted = getPrice() * 0.8;
      discounted = Math.round(discounted * 10) / 10.0;
      return discounted;
    }
    catch (ParseException e)
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
  }

  public int calculateMonthlyPoints(final Customer customer, final String currentMonth)
  {
    if (customer == null || currentMonth == null || currentMonth.isEmpty())
    {
      return 0;
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS))
    {
      return 0;
    }
    int total = 0;
    for (Booking b : customer.getBookings())
    {
      if (b == null)
      {
        continue;
      }
      if (b.isInMonth(currentMonth))
      {
        total += b.getNumberOfSeats() * 5;
      }
    }
    return total;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Computes the final price for a booking made by a given customer at a given booking time. A 20 percent discount is applied only if the customer's membership package contains the DISCOUNTS award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before the trip's departure time (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary). The result is rounded to one decimal place.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null OR bookingTime is null OR this.departureTime is null, return this.price.
   *   2. If customer.membershipPackage is null OR not customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS), return this.price.
   *   3. Parse bookingTime and this.departureTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"; if parsing fails, return this.price.
   *   4. Compute the duration in minutes between bookingTime and departureTime.
   *   5. If duration < 24 * 60 (i.e., less than 24 hours before departure), return this.price.
   *   6. Compute discounted = this.price * 0.8.
   *   7. Round discounted to one decimal place (e.g., using Math.round(discounted * 10) / 10.0).
   *   8. Return discounted.
   * Related Features: price, departureTime
   * Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input:
   *   - customer : Customer - the booking customer; must be non-null to receive a discount.
   *   - bookingTime : String - the booking datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format; must be non-null and parseable.
   * Output: double - the final price after potential discount, rounded to one decimal place; if no discount applies, the original price is returned.
   * Pre-condition: The trip's price and departureTime are set; the customer's membership package, if present, contains valid Award values.
   * Post-condition: No state change occurs; the computation is read-only.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public double calculateDiscountedPrice(final Customer customer, final String bookingTime)
  {
    if (customer == null || bookingTime == null || getDepartureTime() == null)
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS))
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
    SimpleDateFormat format = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    try
    {
      Date bookingDate = format.parse(bookingTime);
      Date departureDate = format.parse(getDepartureTime());
      long durationMinutes = (departureDate.getTime() - bookingDate.getTime()) / (60 * 1000);
      if (durationMinutes < 24 * 60)
      {
        return getPrice();
      }
      double discounted = getPrice() * 0.8;
      discounted = Math.round(discounted * 10) / 10.0;
      return discounted;
    }
    catch (ParseException e)
    {
      return getPrice();
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Computes the total reward points earned by a given customer across all of the customer's bookings during the requested month. Each booked seat contributes 5 points and only customers whose membership package contains the POINTS award are eligible.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null OR currentMonth is null/empty, return 0.
   *   2. If customer.membershipPackage is null OR not customer.membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS), return 0.
   *   3. Initialize total = 0.
   *   4. For each booking b in customer.bookings:
   *        a. If b is null, skip.
   *        b. If b.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true, total += b.numberOfSeats * 5.
   *   5. Return total.
   * Related Features: bookings (of the customer)
   * Related Classes: Customer, Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input:
   *   - customer : Customer - the customer whose points are being calculated; must be non-null.
   *   - currentMonth : String - a textual month identifier, e.g., "yyyy-MM"; must be non-null and non-empty.
   * Output: int - the total points earned for the given month by the given customer; 0 if the customer is not eligible or no bookings qualify.
   * Pre-condition: The customer's bookings, if any, are valid Booking instances with parseable bookingDate values.
   * Post-condition: No state change occurs.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public int calculateMonthlyPoints(final Customer customer, final String currentMonth)
  {
    if (customer == null || currentMonth == null || currentMonth.isEmpty())
    {
      return 0;
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS))
    {
      return 0;
    }
    int total = 0;
    for (Booking b : customer.getBookings())
    {
      if (b == null)
      {
        continue;
      }
      if (b.isInMonth(currentMonth))
      {
        total += b.getNumberOfSeats() * 5;
      }
    }
    return total;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Attempts to commit a seat reservation on this trip by reducing the remaining available seat count. It returns true if the seats were successfully reserved, and false otherwise.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If num <= 0, return false.
   *   2. Compute booked = this.getBookedSeats().
   *   3. If booked + num > this.numberOfSeats, return false.
   *   4. Decrement the remaining available seats of this trip by num (i.e., reduce this.numberOfSeats by the number of currently available seats minus num, so that getBookedSeats() reflects the new reservation). Equivalently, increment the tracked booked count by num, or reduce the remaining seat count by num while keeping total capacity unchanged.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: numberOfSeats, bookings
   * Related Classes: Booking
   * Input:
   *   - num : int - the number of seats to reserve; must be a positive integer.
   * Output: boolean - true if seats were reserved; false if num is non-positive or there are not enough available seats.
   * Pre-condition: The trip has a valid positive numberOfSeats and the bookings list is consistent with the current seat inventory.
   * Post-condition: On success, the trip's remaining available seat count is reduced by num such that getBookedSeats() reflects the new reservation; on failure, no state change occurs.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean bookSeats(final int num)
  {
    if (num <= 0)
    {
      return false;
    }
    int booked = getBookedSeats();
    if (booked + num > getNumberOfSeats())
    {
      return false;
    }
    setNumberOfSeats(getNumberOfSeats() - num);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Determines whether a candidate time window overlaps with this trip's scheduled time window. Overlap is defined as the intervals sharing any positive duration; identical intervals are considered conflicting, but an exact boundary touch (e.g., one trip ends exactly when the other starts) is allowed.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Try to parse this.departureTime, this.arrivalTime, newDepartureTime, and newArrivalTime as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"; if any parsing fails, return false.
   *   2. If this.departureTime >= this.arrivalTime OR newDepartureTime >= newArrivalTime, return false.
   *   3. Return (this.departureTime < newArrivalTime) AND (newDepartureTime < this.arrivalTime).
   * Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input:
   *   - newDepartureTime : String - the proposed departure time in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format.
   *   - newArrivalTime : String - the proposed arrival time in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm" format; must be strictly later than newDepartureTime.
   * Output: boolean - true if the candidate interval overlaps this trip's interval (strict intersection); false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: This trip's departureTime and arrivalTime are valid datetime strings; the proposed times are also valid datetime strings.
   * Post-condition: No state change occurs; the method is read-only.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isTimeConflicting(final String newDepartureTime, final String newArrivalTime)
  {
    SimpleDateFormat format = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    try
    {
      Date thisDeparture = format.parse(getDepartureTime());
      Date thisArrival = format.parse(getArrivalTime());
      Date candidateDeparture = format.parse(newDepartureTime);
      Date candidateArrival = format.parse(newArrivalTime);
      if (!thisDeparture.before(thisArrival) || !candidateDeparture.before(candidateArrival))
      {
        return false;
      }
      return thisDeparture.before(candidateArrival) && candidateDeparture.before(thisArrival);
    }
    catch (ParseException e)
    {
      return false;
    }
  }

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in <Operations> with a specfication.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Driver::canPostTrip
Summary:
  Validates whether a driver is allowed to publish a brand-new trip by
  checking the new trip's time validity and absence of time overlap
  with any of the driver's existing trips.
Algorithm:
  1. If newtrip == null, return false.
  2. If newtrip.departureTime or newtrip.arrivalTime is null or does
     not parse with "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", return false.
  3. If newtrip.departureTime >= newtrip.arrivalTime, return false.
  4. For each existing in this.trips:
       - If existing == null, continue.
       - If existing.isTimeConflicting(newtrip.departureTime,
                                      newtrip.arrivalTime)
         returns true, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features:
  - Driver.trips
  - Trip.departureTime
  - Trip.arrivalTime
  - Trip.isTimeConflicting()
Related Classes:
  - Trip
Input:
  - newtrip : Trip - the candidate trip the driver wants to publish
Output:
  - boolean: true if the trip can be published, false otherwise
Pre-condition:
  - The driver's existing trips list is initialized.
  - newtrip contains parseable datetime strings in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm".
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; pure validation.

Driver::checkStopOverlap
Summary:
  Determines whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share
  at least one common stop station (case-sensitive comparison).
Algorithm:
  1. If trip1 == null OR trip2 == null, return false.
  2. Get stops1 = trip1.getStopStations(), stops2 = trip2.getStopStations().
  3. If stops1 is empty OR stops2 is empty, return false.
  4. For each station in stops1:
       - If stops2 contains the exact same string (case-sensitive),
         return true.
  5. Return false.
Related Features:
  - Trip.stops
  - Trip.getStopStations()
  - Stop.stopStation
Related Classes:
  - Trip, Stop
Input:
  - trip1 : Trip
  - trip2 : Trip
Output:
  - boolean: true if the two trips share at least one stop station
             (case-sensitive), false otherwise (including any null /
             empty-stop-collection case)
Pre-condition:
  - Both arguments are expected to be indirect trips containing stops.
  - The method is null-safe.
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; pure predicate.

# Operation Specifications
Booking::isInMonth
Summary:
  Reports whether the booking's bookingDate falls within the requested
  calendar month (used for monthly reward points computation).
Algorithm:
  1. If bookingDate == null, return false.
  2. Compare the year-month portion of bookingDate with the supplied
     `month` argument (expected format "yyyy-MM").
  3. Return the comparison result.
Related Features:
  - Booking.bookingDate
Related Classes:
  - None
Input:
  - month : String - calendar month in the format "yyyy-MM" (e.g. "2024-03")
Output:
  - boolean: true if bookingDate belongs to `month`, false otherwise
Pre-condition:
  - `month` must follow the "yyyy-MM" pattern; bookingDate may be null.
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; pure predicate.

Booking::updateTripSeats
Summary:
  Applies the booking's effect on the trip's available seat inventory
  by subtracting the booked seats from the trip's seat count.
Algorithm:
  1. If trip == null or numberOfSeats <= 0, return without action.
  2. Call trip.bookSeats(numberOfSeats).
  3. (Optionally) append this booking to trip.bookings if not already present.
Related Features:
  - Booking.trip
  - Booking.numberOfSeats
  - Trip.bookSeats()
  - Trip.bookings
Related Classes:
  - Trip
Input:
  - None
Output:
  - void
Pre-condition:
  - isBookingEligible() must have returned true and trip must still
    have at least numberOfSeats remaining seats.
Post-condition:
  - trip.numberOfSeats is reduced by this booking's numberOfSeats.
  - trip.bookings contains this booking.

Booking::isBookingEligible
Summary:
  Determines whether the current booking satisfies all eligibility rules
  required by the rideshare system so that the trip seat inventory can be
  safely reduced and the booking accepted.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer == null OR trip == null OR bookingDate == null, return false.
  2. Parse trip.departureTime as a datetime using the pattern
     "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm".
  3. Compute the difference between bookingDate and trip.departureTime.
     If the difference is <= 2 hours, return false (must be strictly
     earlier by more than 2 hours).
  4. Compute the remaining seats of the trip as
     trip.numberOfSeats - trip.getBookedSeats().
     If numberOfSeats > remainingSeats, return false.
  5. For every booking already belonging to the customer:
       - If that booking's trip is null, skip it.
       - If overlapsWith(otherTrip) returns true (same calendar day
         AND time intervals overlap), return false.
  6. Return true.
Related Features:
  - Booking.bookingDate
  - Booking.numberOfSeats
  - Booking.customer
  - Booking.trip
  - Booking.overlapsWith()
Related Classes:
  - Customer, Trip
Input:
  - None (operates on the receiver's own fields)
Output:
  - boolean: true if every eligibility condition is satisfied,
             false otherwise (including any null/invalid input case)
Pre-condition:
  - The receiver object is assumed to be fully instantiated; the method
    itself defends against null customer/trip/bookingDate.
  - trip.departureTime is expected to be a string in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm".
Post-condition:
  - Returns true ONLY when the booking can be safely accepted and the
    caller may proceed to invoke updateTripSeats().
  - No state is mutated by this method.

Booking::overlapsWith
Summary:
  Tests whether the time window of the receiver booking's trip overlaps
  with the time window of another given trip on the same calendar day,
  as required by booking-eligibility validation.
Algorithm:
  1. If `trip` is null, return false.
  2. Parse this.trip.departureTime, this.trip.arrivalTime,
     trip.departureTime, and trip.arrivalTime as datetimes
     ("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm").
  3. If the two trips occur on different calendar days, return false.
  4. Define overlap as: max(startA, startB) < min(endA, endB).
     If true, the intervals overlap; return true.
  5. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features:
  - Booking.trip
  - Trip.departureTime
  - Trip.arrivalTime
Related Classes:
  - Trip
Input:
  - trip : Trip - the candidate trip to be compared against this booking's trip
Output:
  - boolean: true if the two trips share any common datetime on the same
             calendar day, false otherwise
Pre-condition:
  - this.trip must be non-null and carry parseable datetime strings.
Post-condition:
  - No state mutation; pure predicate.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

title rideshare Model

}

    customer : Customer

}

    stopStation : String
    trip : Trip
}

    arrivalStation : String
    arrivalTime : String
    departureDate : EDate
    departureStation : String
    departureTime : String
    numberOfSeats : int
    price : double
    bookings : List<Booking>

    getBookedSeats() : int
    getStopStations() : List<String>
    isTimeConflicting(newDepartureTime : String, newArrivalTime : String) : boolean
}

    email : String
    id : String
    phoneNumber : String
}
enum Award {
    CASHBACK
    DISCOUNTS
    POINTS
}

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

title rideshare Model

    trip : Trip

    departureTime : String

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```
